body:
## Problem

When dss runs as a non-root user in a container that also has **any** root process it cannot inspect (here the DinD inner `dockerd`, `containerd` and `sudo`), **every** item is blocked:

```
BLOCKED: "busy: cannot verify process and open-file activity: EACCES: permission denied, readlink '/proc/<pid>/cwd' …"
```

Environment: dss 0.14.1 from `main` (`0c4a695`, run from source with `node bin/dss.js`; npm still has 0.13.1, #19). Host: Ubuntu 24.04, Docker 29.6.1 with the containerd image store. Inside: hive-mind DinD task containers (`konard/hive-mind-dind:2.34.0`, user `box` uid 1001, an inner root `dockerd`), resumed from `docker commit` snapshots after a host dockerd crash. All runs were `scan --no-docker --json --tier moderate` (never deletes) with `DOCKER_HOST=unix:///nonexistent.sock` (#22).

| Container (same image, same user) | inner root dockerd | items | blocked |
|---|---|---|---|
| router#727 task (`175ff931…-resume-1`) | yes | 15 | **15** (incl. 13.9 GiB "safe") |
| router#728 task (`eec34a2b…-resume-1-resume-2`) | yes | 20 | **20** |
| router#724 task (`9243e682…-resume-1-resume-2`) | no | 18 | only real busy ones (cargo running, 1h window) |
| router#727 as root: `docker exec -u 0 -e HOME=/home/box …` | yes | 14 | 1 (npm cache, modified 5 min ago) |

So the same scan is useless or useful depending only on whether an unrelated root daemon runs in the container. #14 and #19 reported "in-container liveness blocks every item" for 0.13.1. This is the same symptom on current `main`, with a different trigger.

## Root cause

`src/env/local.js` → `rawOpenPaths({ strict = true })` throws on the **first** `EACCES`/`EPERM` from `readlink(/proc/<pid>/{cwd,exe,fd/*})` of any process. `openPaths()` then sets `probeDiagnostic`, and `liveness.js` blocks every item with "cannot verify". One unreadable pid disables verification for the whole environment.

## Suggested fix

- Degrade per process, not per environment. Read what *is* readable for unreadable pids (`/proc/<pid>/status` Uid, `cmdline` and `comm` are world-readable). Then block only items that such a process could plausibly use: paths named in its cmdline, its known data roots for recognised daemons (`dockerd`/`containerd` → `--data-root`, `/var/lib/docker`, `/run`; `sudo` → its readable child), and items owned by that uid. Treat all other items as verified by the readable processes.
- Try the existing privileged inspection (`sudo -n`, as in `env/shell.js`) in the local environment too, before giving up.
- When verification is still impossible, print **one** environment-level hint ("N root processes are unreadable; re-run as root, e.g. `docker exec -u 0 -e HOME=$HOME …`") instead of repeating the same blocker on every item.
- Test: a fixture with one unreadable pid must leave unrelated items unblocked.

Workaround: run dss as root with `HOME` pointing at the user's home (`docker exec -u 0 -e HOME=/home/box <container> dss scan …`).

---

We need to download all logs and data related about the issue to this repository, make sure we compile that data to `./docs/case-studies/issue-{id}` folder, and use it to do deep case study analysis (also make sure to search online for additional facts and data), in which we will reconstruct timeline/sequence of events, list of each and all requirements from the issue, find root causes of the each problem, and propose possible solutions and solution plans for each requirement (we should also check known existing components/libraries, that solve similar problem or can help in solutions).

If there is not enough data to find actual root cause, add debug output and verbose mode if not present, that will allow us to find root cause on next iteration.

If issue related to any other repository/project, where we can report issues on GitHub, please do so. Each issue must contain reproducible examples, workarounds and suggestions for fix the issue in code. Also double check to fully apply requirements to entire codebase, so if we have issue in multiple places, it should be fixed in all them.

Please plan and execute everything in this single pull request, you have unlimited time and context, as context auto-compacts and you can continue indefinitely, until it is each and every requirement fully addressed, and everything is totally done.
title: In-container scan as non-root: one unreadable root process (DinD dockerd/sudo) blocks every item with "cannot verify process and open-file activity: EACCES"
